The main takeaway from our work is that

DNA barcodes and metabarcodes are useful tools for studying the interactions between host organisms (plants, insects, etc.) and their symbiotic associates (bacteria, fungi, arthropods, etc.), because they provide a way to rapidly identify individual symbiont species and characterize entire symbiont communities, and because they allow the evolutionary histories and biogeographic distributions of symbionts to be assessed in relation to their host.
